Reduced hours or pay counts as financial hardship. Before asking for any payment, the agent must acknowledge the hardship and record hardship_flag with the stated reason. They must then offer at least one eligible hardship option, such as HP-LOAN-RED3 (pay 50% of the regular payment for 3 months), HP-CARD-MIN (minimum payment halved for 3 months), HP-CARD-RATE (lower interest rate for 6 months), or a skip-a-payment once in 12 months. The agent must also not ask for a payment the customer has said they can't afford. Customers in bankruptcy or a consumer proposal can't get these options.

answer: None of our current collections documents say when the bank can sue or refer a customer to legal action. Nothing in them sets missing two payments as a trigger, so this needs to go to the legal team. Here is what the current policies do say. Agents must never threaten legal action, garnishment or arrest, and must not make misleading statements about consequences (QA checklist items 4 and 5). If the customer says they are in hardship, the agent must acknowledge it, record it and offer at least one eligible hardship option before asking for payment (POL-COLL-004 §4.2). If the customer has filed for bankruptcy or a consumer proposal, a stay of proceedings applies: all collection contact stops from the filing date and the case moves to insolvency_hold (POL-COLL-001 §7.3). If a credit counsellor, lawyer or Licensed Insolvency Trustee represents the customer, all contact goes through that representative (POL-COLL-001 §5.4).

answer: The 3-month reduced payment programme (HP-LOAN-RED3) lasts 3 months. The customer pays 50% of their regular payment, so the payment is cut by half.
